_note: Findings from the scaffold evaluation of devforge-architect (SKILL-005). Severity is chosen from the demonstrated consequence, never from a criterion's label. An evaluation_gap is an evaluation prerequisite owned by someone other than the candidate's author; it is never a defect in the candidate and editing the candidate will not close it. This record contains no digest of itself.

requirement_ids: SKILL-005 'Workflow and phase exits' closing paragraph
findings.location: SKILL.md - no interruption or resume branch exists; the sections where one belongs are 'When something is missing or a check cannot run' (lines 103-111) and 'Stopping' (lines 113-120). Second locus: docs/skill-authoring/history/claude-scaffolding-20260910/devforge-architect/authoring/spec-mapping.md, 'Workflow and phase exits' final row.

evidence.description: Case-insensitive grep for interrupt|resume across every Markdown file in the package returns exactly one hit: the '## Resume and custody' heading inside the copied handoff template. No instruction anywhere addresses an interrupted session.
evidence.locator: commands.log; verification-results.md 'Manual structural observations' row M-11

evidence.description: 'On interruption, preserve the current phase and evidence; resume by checking their identities and the session assignment again.'
'If the worktree or active run changes, re-establish the appropriate baseline and evidence before resuming.'

spec-mapping.md maps this requirement to references/recording-rules.md 'Resolving an upstream reference' and 'When no session record exists'. Those bytes were read. They carry the identity-recheck half as unconditional pre-write rules and do not carry the phase-and-evidence-preservation half, and neither is framed as an interruption or resume path, so a resumed session has no trigger to consult them. The mapping row claims full coverage of a partially carried requirement.

findings.confidence: High that the instruction is absent - the grep is exhaustive over the package. Moderate on the size of the consequence: the unconditional pre-write identity rules would in practice catch the highest-risk resumed-session failure, a silently stale upstream, which is why this is MINOR and not MAJOR. The residual gap is real but narrow.
findings.impact: A session interrupted mid-contract has no instruction to preserve the current phase's partial evidence or to re-read the session assignment before continuing. The observable consequence is a resumed session that carries partial phase work forward without re-establishing the assignment it is writing under - the situation the execution contract's worktree-assignment rules exist to prevent. It does not affect a session that runs to completion in one pass.
findings.recommendation: CHG-001. Add an interruption and resume branch to SKILL.md - two sentences, in 'Stopping' or as a sixth bullet in 'When something is missing or a check cannot run'. Correct the spec-mapping row to say partial with the two halves distinguished.

findings.location: SKILL.md line 3, frontmatter description, exclusion clause; evals/triggers/trigger-queries.json entry A12a and owner_map.negative_review

evidence.description: The authored trigger set carries negative A12a - 'Review this candidate against the story's acceptance criteria and tell me if it is ready' - with owner_map routing it to devforge-review (SKILL-010). The description names seven sibling exclusions and devforge-review is not among them; devforge-release and devforge-evaluate-expert are likewise unnamed.

The description is 1,297 characters. The live Claude Code skills documentation, retrieved 2026-09-10 UTC, states the description (combined with when_to_use) is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing, leaving 239 characters of headroom - enough for a devforge-review clause.

findings.confidence: High on the facts; the effect on selection is unmeasured because tier A did not run. This is a discrimination-margin observation, not a demonstrated misrouting.
findings.impact: A near-miss review request is discriminated only by the absence of an attractor rather than by a stated boundary. No FAIL anchor is met and no required use case is affected, so this does not fail R01.
findings.recommendation: CHG-002, optional. Add a devforge-review exclusion clause to the description within the measured headroom. Do not extend the description past the truncation limit to do it.

requirement_ids: SKILL-005 'Only documented, implemented DevForge commands may be named as executable gates'
findings.location: SKILL.md line 93, 'External checks and what they prove'

evidence.description: SKILL.md says the surface 'includes check, expert prepare|bind|status, init, red, green, accept, verify, status and isolate'. The operator binary devforge 0.1.0 (sha256 835c3263...) lists one further top-level command, `delivery`, with its own subcommands capabilities, init, status, advance, resume, complete, check, verify, run and hook. Every command the package names does exist, and the word 'includes' makes the list non-exhaustive rather than false; the same sentence instructs the reader to run `devforge --help` on the operator's binary.
evidence.locator: commands.log, devforge --help and devforge delivery --help observed 2026-09-10T21:23:15Z-21:27:14Z

findings.confidence: High. This is a completeness observation, not an error: no named command is fabricated and no missing command is needed by this skill's workflow.
findings.impact: None demonstrated. A reader following the instruction to check the operator's binary sees the full surface.
findings.recommendation: No target edit required. If the author touches that sentence for another reason, `delivery` may be added; changing it solely for completeness is not justified by the evidence.

requirement_ids: SKILL-005 'Outputs and standardized templates' consumer-coverage line

evidence.description: The specification's consumer coverage line reads 'architecture-contract -> plan; project-expert-creator; evaluate-expert; develop; review; change.' SKILL.md names plan, project-expert-creator, develop and review; the description names change as the owner of upgrade proposals; devforge-evaluate-expert is named nowhere in the package.
evidence.locator: SKILL.md lines 3 and 87; specification 'Outputs and standardized templates'

evidence.description: spec-mapping.md discloses this as a deliberate partial with a stated reason - evaluate-expert consumes an expert package rather than the contract directly, and naming an uninstalled skill in a continuation would risk presenting it as an available next step. The bytes match the disclosure.
evidence.locator: authoring/spec-mapping.md, 'Outputs and standardized templates' consumer row

findings.confidence: High on the facts. The author's reasoning is defensible and is reinforced by SKILL.md's own instruction to check what is actually installed before naming a skill in a continuation.
findings.impact: None demonstrated. The specification line describes artifact flow across the roster, not an instruction the skill must recite.
findings.recommendation: No target edit. Recorded so the partial coverage is visible to the coordinator as a considered decision rather than an omission.

evidence.description: 22 queries, split fixed at authoring time and recorded once, balanced by should_trigger (7 positive / 7 negative in train, 4 / 4 in validation) and with no duplicate IDs. Every negative category has an owner_map entry and every owner_map entry has a query. However eight of the thirteen categories carry exactly one query, so six negative routings - accepted-story, early-exploration, story-breakdown, ux-design, review and copy-edit for the train-only ones, and scope-definition, expert-authoring and prototype for the validation-only ones - appear in one split only and have no coverage in the other.

findings.confidence: High on the tally. The file's split_policy claims stratification 'by should_trigger and category', which is true in the sense that each category is deterministically assigned; it does not claim per-category presence in both splits.
findings.impact: None demonstrated - tier A did not run. If it later does, six near-miss routings will be evidenced only from the split that happens to contain them, so a description change tuned on train has no held-out check for those six.
findings.recommendation: CHG-005, optional and only if tier A is scheduled. Add one query to the thinner side of the single-entry negative categories. Do not re-randomise the existing split, which is fixed and recorded.

findings.affected_revision: not a property of the candidate
findings.location: the evaluation assignment, not the package

evidence.description: This assignment allocated no installed or exported copy of devforge-architect, no fresh Claude Code terminal, and no permitted isolated evaluation workspace, and the packet directs that no install be attempted. Tiers C, B and A are therefore NOT_RUN with that cause.

findings.confidence: Certain. This is an assignment scope fact, not an inference.
findings.impact: Every behavioural claim about this skill is unavailable: discovery, activation, instruction loading, installed-resource resolution in a consuming project, and output quality against the without_skill baseline. The specification's acceptance requirement - real outputs from representative requests in each supported terminal, with the terminal version, actual discovery/activation, revisions, assignment and evidence location recorded - is entirely unmet. Behavioural status is NOT_EVALUATED.
findings.recommendation: Coordinator to allocate an installed copy, a fresh terminal and an isolated workspace and dispatch a native evaluation. Severity MAJOR reflects the size of the unmet acceptance requirement; it is not a defect in the candidate and no edit to the candidate produces it.

findings.affected_revision: not a property of the candidate
findings.location: the DevForge CLI, owned by the DevForge integration owner

evidence.description: Verified against the operator binary rather than taken on the validator's word: `devforge --help`, `devforge check --help`, `devforge expert --help` and `devforge delivery --help` were run against devforge 0.1.0 sha256 835c3263.... `check` is described as 'Check structural policy and provenance; does not certify semantic behavior' and takes a project and a policy; there is no skill-package inspector, no rule catalogue, no evidence reducer and no protected-manifest custody command anywhere in the surface.

findings.confidence: Certain for this binary at this revision. A future CLI revision could change it; the check must be repeated against the binary actually supplied.
findings.impact: Statement one: skill-package structural inspection (S001-S013) and evidence reduction are not implemented in the DevForge CLI, so every structural row in this evaluation was obtained by reading, is labelled INSPECTION_MANUAL with authority none, and the disposition was adjudicated by hand against the results contract with no decision receipt produced. Statement two: protected-manifest custody for the evaluation runner - binding the runner, graders, runtime, case inputs and grading criteria outside evaluated-agent write access and verifying those identities before acceptance criteria are applied - is not implemented in the DevForge CLI, so the runner and grader identities in every observations header are self-reported by the run. A complete set of matching runner rows does not close either dependency.
findings.recommendation: Route to the DevForge integration owner as an evaluation prerequisite. No candidate edit produces either capability.

findings.affected_revision: not a property of the candidate

evidence.description: The packet designates this session as the fresh evaluator context, and it is separately dispatched from the author. But the same single session ran P2 and P3, and evals/evals.json - which carries the author's own graded_observations, effectively the expected answers for tier B - was read during P2 orientation before R01-R10 were drafted. No second reviewer was dispatched.

findings.confidence: Certain; this is a fact about how the review was conducted.
findings.impact: The R01-R10 records are an independent-of-the-author reading but not a doubly separated one, and they were formed with the author's tier-B expected observations already in context. It does not invalidate the findings - F-001 rests on an exhaustive grep and a specification sentence, neither of which the author's records could have anchored - but a consequential disagreement about any criterion should be resolved with a second fresh reviewer on the same raw packet rather than by weighing this one more heavily.
findings.recommendation: Record the limit. Dispatch a second fresh reviewer only if a criterion outcome becomes contested.
